problem.title: Design a 100M-Trace/Day Enterprise Synthetic Data & Self-Play Pipeline
problem.prompt: Design an enterprise synthetic data generation and verifier-guided self-play pipeline producing 100M+ verified reasoning traces per day across 2,048 H100 GPUs, with <125ms isolated sandbox verification, zero benchmark contamination, step-level PRM filtering, and ACID dataset rollbacks.

spark.summary: Orchestrate 250M+ raw rollouts/day across 2,048 H100s (vLLM/SGLang FP8), verify in <125ms Firecracker microVMs, decontaminate via MinHash LSH + 13-gram Bloom filters, and commit 100M golden traces/day to Apache Iceberg.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, 40% end-to-end verification + PRM yield turns 420 TB/day raw rollouts into 140 TB/day high-signal ACID datasets with sub-second rollback.
spark.byteSummary:
Scale & Yield Math: Producing 100M+ verified traces/day at 40% combined verifier + PRM yield requires 250M+ raw rollouts/day (2,894 sustained / 7,500 peak rollouts/sec) across 2,048 NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs, compressing 420 TB/day raw Parquet ingress into 140 TB/day Apache Iceberg storage.

6-Subsystem Pipeline: (1) Hierarchical 1B+ Seed-Persona DAG Mutator with KL >= 0.72 floor; (2) vLLM/SGLang FP8 Inference Fleet; (3) Firecracker microVM Farm (userfaultfd <125ms restore, zero-egress, Lean4/Pytest/Z3); (4) 128-perm MinHash LSH + 13-gram Bloom filter (<=4ms/1K tokens); (5) PRM Step Scorer (min_t >= 0.78, p95 <=35ms); (6) Apache Iceberg + ClickHouse Telemetry.

Resilience & Governance: Every persisted trace carries batch_id and iceberg_commit_id provenance so contaminated or poisoned batches can be rolled back atomically.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a 100M-Trace/Day Enterprise Synthetic Data & Self-Play Pipeline without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, 40% end-to-end verification + PRM yield turns 420 TB/day raw rollouts into 140 TB/day high-signal ACID datasets with sub-second rollback.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Firecracker Sandbox Farm: <125ms Restore & Fork-Bomb Defense
learningJourney.purpose: Safely run untrusted code and Lean4 proofs at 2,894+ req/s with sub-125ms cold starts.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Firecracker Sandbox Farm: <125ms Restore & Fork-Bomb Defense** as the intuition layer for Design a 100M-Trace/Day Enterprise Synthetic Data & Self-Play Pipeline: Safely run untrusted code and Lean4 proofs at 2,894+ req/s with sub-125ms cold starts.
explanation.core: Each bare-metal verifier host maintains a warm pool of Firecracker microVM snapshots pre-booted with Lean4, GCC 13.2, Rust 1.75, Pytest, SymPy, and Z3. Using `userfaultfd` lazy page restoration hits `<125 ms` startup, while `cgroups v2` (`pids.max`, CPU quota, memory max), `seccomp-bpf`, and zero-egress TAP interfaces neutralize fork bombs and exfiltration.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, firecracker sandbox farm: <125ms restore & fork-bomb defense becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Industrial self-play at 420 TB/day raw -> 140 TB/day Iceberg relies on KL >= 0.72 curriculum mutation, blind property-based sandbox tests, early PRM pruning, and instant snapshot rollbacks.

learningJourney.title: PRM Rejection Sampling & Early-Stop Tree Search
learningJourney.purpose: Score intermediate reasoning steps at <=35ms p95 and prune low-reward branches mid-generation.

learningJourney.title: Poison-Batch Rollbacks via Apache Iceberg & ClickHouse
learningJourney.purpose: Detect model collapse or contaminated batches in real time and roll back 10M+ traces atomically.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Poison-Batch Rollbacks via Apache Iceberg & ClickHouse** as the intuition layer for Design a 100M-Trace/Day Enterprise Synthetic Data & Self-Play Pipeline: Detect model collapse or contaminated batches in real time and roll back 10M+ traces atomically.

knowledgeChecks.question: At 40% combined verification + PRM yield, how many raw rollouts/sec must the 2,048-GPU H100 fleet sustain on average to persist 100M golden traces/day?

options.feedback: Incorrect: 1,157/sec is the net golden commit rate (100M / 86,400), not the raw rollout rate.
Correct: 100M / 0.40 = 250M raw rollouts/day, which equals 250,000,000 / 86,400 = ~2,894 rollouts/sec average.
Incorrect: 250/sec is more than 10x too low for 250M/day.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: 100M verified traces/day at 40% yield requires 250M raw rollouts/day, or ~2,894 rollouts/sec sustained average.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should untrusted model-generated Python/Lean4 code run in userfaultfd-restored Firecracker microVMs rather than standard Docker containers?

options.feedback: Incorrect: Docker runs Python, but shares the host Linux kernel.

options.text: Firecracker automatically proves Lean4 theorems without Lean4.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Firecracker provides hardware virtualization, while Lean4 runs inside the guest.

options.text: Firecracker provides hardware KVM kernel isolation against escapes and restores pre-warmed snapshots via userfaultfd in <125 ms.
options.feedback: Correct: KVM microVMs isolate untrusted syscalls from the host kernel while userfaultfd hits <125ms cold starts.
Incorrect: MicroVMs run with strict cgroups v2 memory and PID limits.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Firecracker combines KVM kernel isolation (blocking container-escape exploits) with <125ms userfaultfd snapshot restoration.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the pipeline simultaneously deduplicate 250M daily rollouts and block benchmark leakage without O(N^2) comparisons?

options.text: 128-permutation MinHash LSH (32x4 bands, J >= 0.80) for near-duplicates plus a rolling-hash 13-gram Bloom filter against held-out eval sets.
options.feedback: Correct: LSH handles near-duplicate clustering in sub-linear time while the 13-gram Bloom filter flags eval overlap in <=4ms/1K tokens.

options.text: Exact string equality against every trace in S3.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Exact string matching misses paraphrases and scales poorly.

options.text: Manual human review of all 250M rollouts.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Manual review is impossible at 250M traces/day.
Incorrect: Disabling temperature worsens duplication and causes mode collapse.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Combining 128-permutation MinHash LSH with a 13-gram Bloom filter catches both paraphrases and exact benchmark overlaps at streaming speed.
